## Summary

**Search process:**
- Declared three stopping rules upfront (best_so_far_above 1.2 → stop, failures_at_least 3 → stop, last_gain_at_most 0.02 → restart), and named a parsimony-based prior (feature 0) before any data-driven move.
- `init` anchored on feature 32 (Sharpe 0.385), then `extend_best` found [32+, 35−] at 0.483.
- A 3rd-feature extension consistently *hurt* performance, triggering the last_gain restart rule repeatedly.
- Ran 5 independent restarts (anchors: 32, 33, 18, 16, 19). All of them, when extended, converged toward pairing with feature 35 (short) as the strongest second leg, and **[33+, 35−]** emerged as the best 2-feature combination (Sharpe 0.491 all-years / 0.554 recent-weighted) — robustly reproduced, never beaten by any 3-feature variant.
- Adjusted the restart trigger's threshold once (logged) when it fired too eagerly on small positive gains, and later changed its action to `stop` once the evidence of a stable optimum was overwhelming, rather than keep restarting into diminishing returns.

**Decision:** Compared against the baseline model (Sharpe 0.183/0.246, turnover 0.042) — the discovered rule beat it by a wide margin on both weightings, so I submitted the **rule** [33+, 35−].

**Prediction:** Mean annualized net Sharpe **0.32**, SD **0.22** — roughly 60-65% of the in-sample figure, reflecting confidence from the rule's robustness (independently rediscovered from 5 different starting points, and resistant to added complexity) tempered by standard caution about in-sample-to-out-of-sample Sharpe decay from any search process.
